A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeurELA research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including the additional Appendix B in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, fine-tuning results, feature visualizations, computational timings, and optimizer and model-complexity comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds DeepELA comparisons, training-convergence results, and an analysis of correlations between learned and traditional landscape features.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and A.1 retain the same normalization and embedding, two-stage attention, positional encoding, pooling, neuroevolution objective, and zero-shot and fine-tuning procedures. The expanded architectural comparison with DeepELA does not introduce a NeurELA method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use BBOB, BBOB-Noisy, and Protein-Docking with the same eight MetaBBO algorithms. The added correlation analysis reuses BBOB-10D and three existing training algorithms; it does not introduce a new task, domain, or input-environment scenario.

E2.justification: v2 compares NeurELA with Original and traditional ELA in Figure 3. v3 adds the learned DeepELA comparator across all eight algorithms and three benchmark suites, substantially strengthening the central comparison set. The evolution-strategy and MLP comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a feature-analysis protocol using three algorithms, all 24 BBOB-10D problems, 500-step trajectories, and Pearson correlations between 16 NeurELA and 32 ELA features. Existing benchmark splits, function-evaluation budgets, model configurations, and performance metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands supplementary analysis beyond the retained PCA visualization and optimizer/model-complexity studies. Appendix B.1 adds training-convergence curves for five evolution strategies, while B.3 adds a broad trajectory-based analysis of correspondence between learned and traditional features.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 specifies 10 independent optimization runs per algorithm/problem and averages per-trajectory Pearson coefficients over 720 trajectories. Figure 10 newly displays training error bars without defining them. The existing 50 evaluation runs, 10 meta-training runs, and Figure 3 bootstrap confidence-interval practice remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds 24 DeepELA results while retaining the existing methods' values. For example, on DEDDQN with BBOB, v3 adds DeepELA's 1.42 beside NeurELA's unchanged 3.03 on the exponentiated relative-performance scale. New convergence curves and the 32-by-16 correlation matrix further expand the reported findings.

T1.justification: The task-space definitions, objectives, normalized performance measure, and attention computations in Equations (1)-(6) are unchanged. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs; the new Pearson-correlation analysis is empirical rather than a theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: automatic dynamic landscape analysis, generalization across MetaBBO tasks, and fine-tuning adaptation. The expanded title clarifies the existing scope, and the added experiments support retained claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v3 links DeepELA's performance to its training objective and adds interpretations identifying supposedly novel or ELA-aligned NeurELA features. Appendix B.3 also suggests that convexity and local-landscape features are less useful for MetaBBO. The existing limitation concerning inefficient neuroevolution training remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 changes the parallel-computation explanation from GPUs to CPUs, consistent with the CPU setup already stated in both versions. Appendix B.3 documents trajectory construction and feature selection. Existing hyperparameters and software licenses remain; the public and anonymous code links merely exchange locations between the abstract and Appendix A.4.

R1.justification: DeepELA was already cited and discussed in v2. v3 expands this focused comparison in Section 2 and Appendix B.2, explaining differences in dimensional embedding, attention workflow, and training objectives. The cited-work set is retained; bibliography reordering and author-year citations are stylistic changes.

P1.justification: v3 expands the title, adds publication information and acknowledgments, clarifies introductory explanations, corrects research-question labels, and introduces Appendix B. The existing section sequence and most prose remain intact, with no extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains DeepELA bars and a legend entry, and Figures 10 and 11 add convergence and correlation displays. The retained plots preserve their content. The ICLR template changes typography, headers, spacing, and float placement, while Figure 4's caption is shortened.

improvement.justification: The DeepELA comparison in Figure 3 addresses a relevant missing empirical comparator, and Figure 10 strengthens support for optimizer selection. These gains are limited by sparse DeepELA implementation details and problematic interpretation in Appendix B.3: feature novelty and usefulness are inferred from correlations described as weak despite strong negative values in Figure 11.
